brief: UBS S&T: the post-election bounce is unwinding momentum and semiconductors as investors rotate into quality and defensive growth. Midterms (Democratic Congress control, anti-data-center governors) pull the AI capacity 'peak in 2028/29' debate forward to 2027: tighter data-center rules could push hyperscalers to front-load capacity, power and permits, raising the risk of an earlier EPS rollover in semis, or could elongate the cycle. About 30% of 2028 data-center additions, including 18 GW in Texas, are flagged at risk. Flows favor hyperscalers (Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, Lam Research) over neoclouds and weaker names (Intel, ServiceNow, CoreWeave, AMD, Sandisk). Oil fell about 10% on Iran de-escalation hopes, cushioning indices and pressuring gold's rally above $4,000, a relief rally UBS says, not a breakout. Hedge funds made their third-largest exposure cut this year even with midterms, Q3 earnings and the October Fed behind them. UBS expects the BoE to hike 25bp to 4.0% Thursday then pause before one more hike to 4.25% in February; BoJ minutes point to a December hike; the RBA hiked to 4.85% amid tension over a deputy governor's pre-meeting signal. ARM fell despite an EPS beat, on a royalty miss and an unraised AGI CPU revenue target.
